questions.question: What is scarcity?
choices: A temporary drop in one product's price
Limited resources relative to people's wants
The absence of any available technology
A government's annual budget deficit

questions.question: What does economics primarily study?
choices: The allocation of scarce resources
Only the design of government buildings
Only the sequence of historical wars
The naming of physical landforms

questions.question: Which is an example of a productive resource?
choices: A worker's labor
A consumer's preference
A retailer's sale price
A customer's demand

questions.question: What does capital mean as a factor of production?
choices: All income received by consumers
Every natural resource below ground
Tools, equipment, and buildings used to produce goods
Only currency held in a wallet

questions.question: What is an incentive?
choices: A resource that has no alternative use
A potential reward or penalty that influences choices
A product available without any cost
An accounting total of past purchases

questions.question: What is a service?
choices: An activity performed to meet a want or need
A physical item held in inventory
A raw material extracted from land
A machine used in production

questions.question: What is specialization?
choices: Producing everything one consumes independently
Dividing resources equally regardless of skills
Avoiding exchange with other producers
Focusing production on particular tasks or products

questions.question: Why do households make trade-offs?
choices: Every choice offers identical benefits
Money eliminates all resource limits
Time, income, and resources have alternative uses
Only businesses face constraints

questions.question: Why can voluntary exchange benefit both participants?
choices: Each expects to gain something valued more than what is given up
Both must receive the same physical item
Trade always eliminates production costs
Prices always remain unchanged after trade

questions.question: Why can specialization raise productivity?
choices: It requires every worker to perform every task
Practice and division of tasks can improve efficiency
It prevents the use of tools
It removes the need for coordination

questions.question: What does a production possibilities frontier illustrate?
choices: Only the prices consumers pay in stores
The dates when national budgets are passed
The distribution of voting rights across a population
Trade-offs in producing two goods with given resources and technology

questions.question: What does a point inside a production possibilities frontier indicate?
choices: The economy has exceeded its productive capacity
Opportunity cost has disappeared
Resources are unemployed or used inefficiently
Every worker is producing at maximum efficiency

questions.question: How does technological improvement affect productive capacity?
choices: It can allow more output from available resources
It necessarily reduces every worker's income
It removes all scarcity permanently
It leaves all production possibilities unchanged

questions.question: Why should decision-makers consider marginal benefits and costs?
choices: Every choice must be evaluated only as all-or-nothing
Choices often involve whether to do a little more or less
Past costs can always be recovered
Average costs always equal additional costs

questions.question: Why is entrepreneurship considered a factor of production?
choices: It measures the total price of every product
It guarantees that every business earns a profit
It eliminates the need for labor and materials
It organizes resources and involves taking business risks

questions.question: A student uses an hour for studying instead of paid work. What is part of the opportunity cost?
choices: Every dollar the student has ever earned
The wages of all classmates
The forgone earnings from that hour of work
Only the price of the student's textbook

questions.question: A baker buys an oven for bread production. Which factor is the oven?
choices: Capital
Labor
Land
Entrepreneurship

questions.question: A firm trains workers and output per hour rises. What changed?
choices: The inflation rate necessarily
Productivity
The exchange rate necessarily
The unemployment definition

questions.question: One more hour of practice offers a benefit worth $15 and a cost worth $8. What does marginal analysis suggest?
choices: The extra hour necessarily has no benefit
Only previous practice costs matter
The cost must equal the benefit
The extra hour has a positive net benefit

questions.question: Which statement is a positive economic claim that could be tested?
choices: The government ought to tax luxury goods more
Every worker deserves the same wage
A price increase was followed by lower sales
The fairest economy distributes income equally
